newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cardoso popularity on the rise - poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cardoso popularity on the rise - poll.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has achieved the highest approval rating since taking office two years ago, according to a newspaper poll.

The survey of 12,510 voters shows 47 percent approve of Cardoso's administration, 38 percent say it is average and only 12 percent disapprove, Folha de Sao Paulo said. Three percent said they did not know.
One month after Cardoso took office in January 1995, only 36 percent approved of his government and 35 percent considered his administration to be average.

Of those interviewed, 76 percent thought the anti-inflation Real Plan, introduced in July 1994, was good for Brazil, slightly down from the 79 percent who approved of the plan in December 1994, Folha de Sao Paulo said.
Approval ratings for Brazil's Congress were lower than for Cardoso's administration, with only 21 percent of those polled saying the work of deputies and senators was good, Folha de Sao Paulo said.
Forty-five percent considered the work of Congress to be average, 26 percent disapproved and eight percent did not know.
(--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151)
